title.narrative: Multinational - Projet de système de paiement de la Zone monétaire de l’Afrique de l’ouest (Gambie, Guinée, et Sierra Leone)
Multinational - West African Monetary Zone Payment System Development Project (The Gambia, Guinea and Sierra Leone)

description.narrative: Les bénéficiaires du projet seront : l'ensemble de la population des quatre pays de la ZMAO - dont une majorité de femmes - (grâce à une participation accrue au secteur financier formel) ; les banques commerciales et les entreprises du secteur privé - en particulier les petites et moyennes entreprises - (grâce à des transferts de fonds plus efficaces).

Project beneficiaries will include: the entire population of the four WAMZ countries - of which a majority are women - (through increased participation in the formal financial sector); and commercial banks, and private sector businesses – especially small and medium enterprises -, (through more efficient transfers of funds).

Le projet vise à améliorer l'infrastructure de base du secteur financier dans la zone monétaire de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (ZMAO) par la mise à niveau des systèmes de paiement de quatre pays de la zone : La Gambie, la Guinée, la Sierra Leone et le Liberia. Lorsque le projet de développement du système de paiement de la ZMAO a été conçu en 2008, le Liberia n'était pas prêt à participer en raison d'autres priorités liées à la réhabilitation post-conflit. Depuis que le Libéria est devenu membre de la ZMAO en février 2010, la facilité de don supplémentaire vise à étendre la mise en œuvre du projet de développement du système de paiement de la ZMAO au Libéria. Le projet comprend les éléments clés suivants : (i) Règlement brut en temps réel (RTGS) ; (ii) Automatisation des paiements de détail (APD) ; (iii) Application de banque centrale (ABC) ; (iv) Mise à niveau de l'infrastructure ; et (v) Gestion du projet. Les résultats attendus du projet comprennent une participation accrue des entreprises du secteur privé et des citoyens de la Gambie, de la Guinée, de la Sierra Leone et du Liberia au secteur financier formel, ainsi qu'une efficacité accrue des transferts de fonds entre les quatre États membres de la ZMAO.

The project aims to improve the basic infrastructure of the financial sector in the West African Monetary Zone (WAMZ) region through the upgrade of the payment systems of four countries in the zone: The Gambia, Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Liberia. At the time the WAMZ Payments System Development Project was designed in 2008, Liberia, was not ready to participate owing to other priorities of post-conflict Rehabilitation. Since Liberia acceded as a member of the WAMZ in February 2010, the supplementary grant facility aims to extend the implementation of the WAMZ Payments System Development Project to Liberia. The project comprises the following key components: (i) Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS); (ii) Retail Payments Automation (RPA); (iii) Central Banking Application (CBA); (iv) Infrastructure Upgrade; and (v) Project management. Expected project outcomes include increased participation of the private sector businesses, and the citizens of The Gambia, Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Liberia in the formal financial sector, and enhanced efficiency of funds transfers across the four WAMZ member states.

L'objectif sectoriel de la ZMAO est de parvenir à une union économique et monétaire complète de ses six États membres : Nigeria, Ghana, Gambie, Guinée, Sierra Leone et Liberia, afin de favoriser un environnement plus propice à une croissance tirée par le secteur privé. L'objectif principal du projet en cours est d'augmenter les systèmes de paiement en Gambie, en Guinée et en Sierra Leone afin d'améliorer la performance de leurs systèmes financiers. En plus d'approfondir les secteurs financiers de ces pays, le projet vise à favoriser l'augmentation des investissements privés grâce à l'amélioration de l'efficacité de l'intermédiation financière. En outre, le projet facilitera le processus de lancement d'une union monétaire dans la zone et stimulera l'accroissement des relations économiques et commerciales dans la région.

The sector goal for WAMZ is to achieve full economic and monetary union of its six member states: Nigeria, Ghana, The Gambia, Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Liberia, to foster a more conducive environment for private sector-led growth. The primary objective of the ongoing project is to augment the payment systems in The Gambia, Guinea, and Sierra Leone in order to enhance the performance of their financial systems. In addition to deepening these countries’ financial sectors, the project aims to foster increased private investment through improved efficiency of financial intermediation. Further, the project will facilitate the process for the launch of a monetary union in the Zone, and would stimulate increased economic and trade relations in the region.

target.value: Volume of high value funds transfers in the four countries increases by 45% from 1,370 in 2007 to 2,000 by 2012.

actual.value: Analyzing data presented by WAMZ as shown in the table below indicates that the combined volume of high and low value funds transfers per checks increased by 18,178% from 4,884 (1,370+3,514) in 2007 to 892,710 as of 2015.

title.narrative: Increased share of intra trade to total trade

actual.value: As of 2015, the Gambia’s share of trade was 5,18%, that of Guineas was 8,89%, Liberia was 5,37% and Sierra Leone was 1%.

title.narrative: Clearing cycle in number of days of local and upcountry checks in the four countries reduced

actual.value: Clearing has improved from 10-14 days on average to T+1, thus clearing cycle target as expected from the outcome of the project has been exceeded

title.narrative: Automation of information technology (IT) systems in four countries’ Central Banks

target.value: The Central Banks in the four countries are disposed of modern IT systems capable of interfacing with the new payment systems in 2011

actual.value: Core Banking Application in all the Central Banks have been upgraded and several processes such as banking services, including customers and account information, teller operations, transfers, money market operations, fund transfers and postings has been automated.

title.narrative: Percentage of the citizens with access to the formal financial services

actual.value: Data is not readily available to measure progress per access to formal financial services. Scanty data available at the World Bank’s database reports Access to Finance for Adults in Guinea as of 2014 at 7%, and Women Adults at 4,1%. For Sierra Leone, Access to Finance for Adults at 2014 was reported as 15,6%, with that of Women reported as 12,5%. In Liberia Access to Finance for Adult per the World Bank was 7% as of 2012.

title.narrative: Deeper financial sector integration in the West African Monetary Zone (WAMZ) region

target.value: Level of financial depth as measured by broad money supply (M2) as a percentage of GDP increases from 20% in 2007 to 30% by 2015

actual.value: For the Gambia, M2 as % of GDP was 56,3% as of 2014 and 56,78% as of 2017. In 2015, that of Guinea was 27,01%, Liberia was 35,7% and Sierra Leone was 24,15%, thus on average, the project has met its financial sector integration impact target.

target.value: High value funds transfers in the four countries effected through RTGS systems and not by bank checks in 2012.

actual.value: High Value Funds Transfer Through RTGS Achieved in the Gambia in 2012, Guinea in 2016, Liberia in 2016 and Sierra Leone in 2013.

title.narrative: Automation of check processing and clearing

target.value: New check standards implemented in the four countries in 2011.

actual.value: New Check Standards Implemented in the Gambia in 2012, Guinea in 2016, Liberia in 2016, and Sierra Leone in 2013. Check Standards has been harmonized in all the six WAMZ countries

title.narrative: Automation of high value funds transfers

target.value: Harmonized payments system law enacted by parliaments in the four countries by end 2011

actual.value: Payment Systems Law Passed in the Gambia in 2012, Guinea Payments Systems Law is pending with parliament, Liberia Payments Systems Law passed in 2014, and Sierra Leone in 2013 (WAMI is working with the member countries to harmonize the regional payments system laws).

title.narrative: Telecommunication infrastructure and standby generators installed at the four Central Banks

target.value: Telecommunication infrastructure for the new payments system, and standby generators for supplementary power supply, are installed by 2011

actual.value: Telecommunication infrastructure for the new payment systems, and standby generators for supplementary power supply, were installed in the Gambia in 2012, Guinea in 2016, Liberia in 2016, and Sierra Leone in 2013.
